source_text: Quid ergo egerimus appareat: omnes plurimos Apostolus dixit, quos ideo ait obnoxios morti, quoniam voluntate propria peccaverunt. Non igitur originale, sed voluntarium crimen accusat; et re vera nihil aliud indicant verba, si eorum fides et proprietas expendatur. Nam si peccatum crederet ad posteros generatione transisse, id est ad eos, qui ibi non fuerant, ab illo fuisse iaculatum, falsissime omnes peccasse pronuntiaret.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore we have done let it appear: the Apostle said all very many, whom he says liable to death for this reason, since they sinned by their own will. He therefore accuses not an original but a voluntary crime; and in truth the words indicate nothing else, if their faith and property are weighed. For if he believed that sin had passed to posterity by generation, that is had been thrown by that one to those who had not been there, he would most falsely pronounce that all had sinned.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Let our result be plain: by ‘all,’ the apostle meant very many, whom he says are subject to death because they sinned by their own will. He therefore accuses voluntary crime, not original crime. In fact, if the words’ reliability and proper meaning are weighed, they indicate nothing else. For if he believed sin passed to descendants by generation—that is, was hurled from Adam at people who had not been there—he would speak utterly falsely in declaring that all sinned (compare Romans 5:12).

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
